About.HowItWorks1: Escape from Tarkov writes your position and camera rotation into the filename of every screenshot you take. This app watches that folder and reads the filenames. Nothing else.
About.HowItWorks2: It does not read the game's memory, hook into the process, modify any game file, or communicate with the game in any way. It cannot see anything you have not already captured yourself.
About.MapGeometry: Map geometry is taken from tarkov-dev, which is MIT licensed. Map artwork remains the work of its authors, credited above.
About.MapsIntro: All map artwork and point-of-interest data comes from the tarkov.dev community project. This app is not affiliated with them; it simply uses what they publish.
About.Stack: Avalonia 11 and SkiaSharp on .NET 8. SVG maps are rendered with Svg.Skia. Everything on the map is custom-drawn.

Prefs.GameLogIntro: Escape from Tarkov writes a plain text log while it runs, and it names the map it is loading up to two minutes before you have control. Reading it means the second monitor is already on the right map when you spawn. Nothing is written and nothing is injected; this only opens a file the game has already saved to disk.
Prefs.GuideLineHint: Used only while the line is pointing at an exit. Routing you along your own markers keeps it pink, so the two are never confused.
prefs.language.restart: Restart the app to apply the new language.
Prefs.LevelFromLog: Work out my level from the game's log
Prefs.LevelFromLogHint: Your level is in no log Tarkov writes. What is knowable is a floor: a quest requiring level 42 cannot have been accepted at 41, so the highest requirement among the quests the log has seen you take is a level you are at least at. It is only ever raised, never lowered, and it lags behind the truth by however far you have got since your hardest quest.
Prefs.LevelHint: Type the real number in if you know it. Only the Quests tab's level filter uses it.
